entry.dc:title: Escondida: evolution of a mine plan.
entry.dc:creator: Hickman R.N.
entry.dc:description: The various phases involved in the mine planning for the Escondida deposit in N Chile are described. Initial plans considered underground development as well as an open pit mine. A final decision was made to proceed with a 35 000 tonnes per day operation. The size of the operation was influenced by an analysis of the growth of copper consumption, by the need to obtain financing and by the availability of such financing. Much of the mine planning was done by hand and later refined by computer methods. Escondida is the best copper project in the world; its development programme and mine planning effort provide a classic example of the relationship between the various business and physical factors required for successful mine development.-J.M.H.

entry.dc:title: HIGHWALL STABILITY MONITORING AT SYNCRUDE CANADA LTD. OPEN PIT MINING OPERATION.
entry.dc:creator: Fair A.
entry.dc:description: The Syncrude Canada Ltd. open pit mine is located approximately 40 km north of Ft. McMurray in northern Alberta. The mining operation utilizes draglines to excavate the oil sands in a single bench operation with up to 60 meter high cuts. The permit level of daily production is 129,000 barrels of synthetic crude oil, and the mine production over the 25-year mine life is in the order of 265,000 tons per day. Since production startup in June 1977, potential slope instability problems have been identified that could affect the safety of the draglines. Four main types of instability have been identified to date. Of these, shallow block slides are considered to be the most hazardous and result from the presence of adversely dipping clay beds within the upper 20 m of the highwall face. The highwall monitoring techniques currently being utilized have evolved over the past 10 years, beginning with the original Test Pit program in 1973-74. Current routine monitoring methods involve vertical slope inclinometers and visual observation. These methods are intermittent and manpower intensive. A review of currently available monitoring methods has shown that traditional surface techniques are not feasible with Syncrude's current mining configuration.

entry.dc:title: Determination of Criteria for Selection of Safety Factors for Coal Open Pit Mine Slopes.
entry.dc:creator: Obradovic R.
entry.dc:description: The criteria for selection of safety factors of coal open pit mine slopes are differently treated and variably defined in preparation of investment technical documentation. The paper deals with additional factors such as the operating stage, flow sheet characteristics, proximity of important facilities and measures undertaken for artificial improvement of stability. A general safety factor corrected F //g//e//n//e//r//a//l, is defined on the basis of additional criteria. After opening of the deposit and the additional study of existing natural conditions, corrections of slope angles and other additional calculations should be made in the basis of investigations and monitoring of the slope state.

entry.dc:title: APPLICATION OF BUCKET WHEEL EXCAVATORS IN A PHILIPPINE CONTINUOUSLY OPERATED OPEN PIT MINE.
entry.dc:creator: Wimmer K.
entry.dc:description: The present paper describes the geological and hydrological conditions of the Unong deposit situated in the Southeast of the Semirara island, approx. 270 km south of Manila. Also, the planning of the open pit mine will be dealt with in detail and the technical data of the equipment will be given. All equipment has been installed during an erection period of twelve months. Production - in three-shift operation - was started in mid 1984.

entry.dc:title: Mass Rates of Combustion of Brown Coal Dust from the Brieske Open Pit Mine.
entry.dc:creator: Karcz H.
entry.dc:description: The problem of determination of the coal grain burning rate has not yet been completely solved theoretically. It is therefore necessary to determine this value experimentally. One of the simplest and most reliable methods is the experiment which is based on the determination of the combustion times of grains of a certain size and a certain mass. The research material obtained is a basis for devising a calculation method that would permit determination of mass rates of individual coal combustion phases. The calculation formulas presented describe the fundamental physicochemical phenomena of the combustion process which it was possible to measure under the given experimental conditions and with the measuring equipment employed.

entry.dc:title: Locating Equidistant Elevations in the Open Pit Mines.
entry.dc:creator: Noaghi T.
entry.dc:description: The authors present an improved method for locating equidistant elevations on the bermes of an open pit mine, in order to evaluate the volumes for production monitoring. A mathematical model for specifying the elevation and determination of elevation intersections with a topographic polygonal contour, without prviously imposed conditions, is described.

entry.dc:title: AUTOMATION OF BUCKET WHEEL EXCAVATORS.
entry.dc:creator: Mason E.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: The requirement to operate bucket wheel excavators closer to the limits of theoretical effective capacity without causing overloads as well as the requirement to generate a stable material flow at any defined level up to design capacity have increased the demand for automated bucket wheel excavators. A continuous 10-year period of development with automatic excavators in the open pit mine has yielded the current version of the automation system consisting of a basic automatic with diagnostic system and options for laser bed leveling and laser output volume. With the present automation system, operational stoppages have been reduced, and it is possible to define any stable material flow up to the design capacity of the excavator. In addition, the material flow has to a large degree become independent of negative weather influences such as rain and fog.

entry.dc:title: Designing Rows of Filter Wells with the Aid of the TAFEGA II Computer Program.
entry.dc:creator: Haenel U.
entry.dc:description: The article describes the EDV-Program TAFEGA II for open pit mine drainage. The program is based on the simulation of boundary conditions of the pipe flow method. The geohydraulic models are successfully developed by this program.

entry.dc:title: Open-pit mine planning and computerized evaluation of china clay reserves in Devon and Cornwall.
entry.dc:creator: Howe J.H.
entry.prism:publicationName: High Heat Production Hhp Granites Hydrothermal Circulation and Ore Genesis
entry.dc:description: A continuous programme of drilling has been conducted since the mid 1950's, resulting in a vast data base, constantly expanding and becoming increasingly difficult to handle. A computerized reserve evaluation system was considered essential to enable a quick response and a detailed and continual update of the Company's reserves. Because of the increasing requirement for sophisticated open-pit mine planning, a multi-disciplinary team was formed to handle all aspects of open pit mine planning; including geology, reserves, mining engineering, slope stability, design draughting and economics. -J.M.H.

entry.dc:creator: Paliwal H.

entry.dc:title: RECENT DEVELOPMENTS AT THE SCHEELITE MINE IN MITTERSILL.
entry.dc:creator: Spross M.
entry.dc:description: Since the discovery of the scheelite deposit at Mittersill in 1967, this mining operation has become one of the largest in the western world. The open pit mine will be closed in 1985 so that the total production of 450,000-500,000 tons is expected to be mined underground. Indications on the ore reserves as of December, 1983, are made. In 1981/1982, a conveyor tunnel between mill and mine was built. The whole crushing plant will be transferred underground so that in the future a material no larger than 15 mm is delivered to the preparation plant on a belt conveyor. A new tailings pond was built near Stuhlfelden, 10 km from the ore preparation plant. Operating data for the slurry pipeline which has been in operation since 1983 are given.

entry.dc:title: Crustal structure of southwestern Montana and east‐central Idaho: Results of a reversed seismic refraction line
entry.dc:creator: Sheriff S.D.
entry.dc:description: On October 20, 1982, we collected seismic refraction data on a 250 km line segment between Butte, Montana and Challis, Idaho. These data are from two open pit mine blasts; one at Anaconda Minerals Companys' southeast Berkely pit and the other at Cyprus Mines Corporations' Thompson creek mine. Eight of our ten recorders wrote clear records of both blasts with measured travel times accurate to +/−0.2 seconds. We supplemented these data with data from permanent stations in the Butte area. The Pg (crustal) velocity is 5.8 km/s to the southwest and 6.0 km/s to the northeast. The Pn (mantle) velocity is 7.9 km/s to the northeast and 8.1 km/s to the southwest; total travel‐times are equal. The S‐wave velocity in the crust is about 3.5 km/s. The symmetry of the travel‐time results, with their intersection within one kilometer of the midpoint between the pit blasts, strongly suggests the refraction line overlies a horizontal Moho or parallels the strike line of a dipping Moho surface. These data indicate the crust in southwestern Montana and east‐central Idaho is approximately 33 km thick. Contrasting tectonic processes, compression and thickening during the Laramide orogeny with extension and thinning since the Paleocene, resulted in a crust with slightly less than normal thickness. entry.dc:title: HYDROLOGIC SITE SELECTION FOR MINING OF DEEP BASIN LIGNITE IN TEXAS.
entry.dc:creator: Charbeneau R.
entry.prism:publicationName: Technical Report University of Texas at Austin Center for Research in Water Resources
entry.dc:description: Texas lignite will be the fuel preferred by many of the state's utilities and industries. Near surface lignite reserves are adequate to meet the needs of the early decades of the 21st century. Meeting the demands of the decades beyond will require the recovery of deep basin lignite or a transition to alternative energy fuels. The subject of this research is the hydrological and geomechanical feasibility and impact of open pit mining and underground coal gasification for recovery of deep basin Texas lignite. Of major concern are the quantities and uses of water from site dewatering and depressurizing operations, the stability of open pit mine slopes and how it is influenced by water, and the regional hydrologic impacts of lignite mining. Refs.

entry.dc:title: On the computation of resection results by least squares
entry.dc:creator: Corbyn J.A.
entry.dc:description: Position fixing by resection within a surveyed area requires a minimum of instrument work and a considerable amount of calculation. A computer/desktop calculator method is described which involves a least square solution and reconciliation between the various sources of error. This is intended to overcome the principal drawback to the use of resection; the practical difficulty with the calculations when more than three points are observed and when the observed points are at widely differing distances. Applications are given in open pit mine surveying and determination of ground movements for slope stability work. © 1983 Maney Publishing.
